newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea riot police fire tear gas at strikers.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea riot police fire tear gas at strikers.

text.p: South Korean riot police fired volleys of tear gas to halt a march by thousands of striking workers in Seoul on Saturday, witnesses said.

It was the first violent clash between strikers and authorities since industrial action began sweeping the nation on Thursday in protest at the secret passage of a new labour law that allows worker layoffs.
Witnesses said around 5,000 demonstrators wearing red and blue protest headbands gathered in a Seoul park to denounce the President Kim Young-sam's government for ramming through the legislation.
After chanting anti-government slogans for three hours in a peaceful protest they tried to march down busy city thoroughfares to Myongdong Cathedral.
Riot police unleashed barrages of tear gas to stop the procession, witnesses said.

The rally was organised by the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions. The government has condemned the strikes as illegal and threatened unspecified "punishment" but has so far shown restrain in handling some of the worst industrial strife since the late 1980s.
